subject: 🏃 Saturday — 3 mi Shakeout + Strides (Wk 5)
html:
Tomorrow: 3 mi shakeout at 9:30+/mi with 4×20-second strides (near-sprint, full recovery between) — a leg-opener after three days off. Pre-run: 5-min activation (quadruped hip CARs, banded lateral walks, glute bridges) plus PT-prescribed quadruped banded hip IR (5–10 reps each side).

Keep the 3 miles genuinely easy on flat ground — the strides do the neuromuscular waking, the jog is just a flush. Your knee logged 2/5 after Wednesday's heavy strength in Boston (mild awareness on stairs, resolved quickly); three days of rest should have cleared it, but check the first few steps. If anything is still talking, drop the strides and swap the run for a 30-min easy walk.

Focus cue: this is a systems check, not a workout. Feel your legs out after the Boston travel week and report back how the knee reads — that 2/5 was the first non-1 reading of the entire V6 build, and Sunday's session depends on where it lands tomorrow.

You're in Week 5 of 12, Phase 2 (Strength & Threshold) — 50 days to the SF Marathon. The real session is Sunday: 12 mi long run on Bayfront flat with a fast-finish (last 2 mi @ MP 7:35–7:45 by HR 150–160), your first 90 g/hr gut training rehearsal, and the Phase 2 volume kickoff. The fast-finish is gated: knee must be 1/5 AND the fuel has to be going down clean — otherwise you run all 12 easy. Tomorrow's shakeout primes you for that.

Tonight: lay out your run kit, charge the watch, confirm the H10 strap is ready (don't repeat May 24), and start planning your Sunday fuel for the 90 g/hr rehearsal. Bed by 10.
